Toolbox

↕ Scroll page

Drag a thing into the world. It stays under your finger while you hold it, and when you let go it falls onto whatever is below. Dreamcap mushrooms can produce waking dreams; hatchlings are extremely vulnerable. Repeated eating builds slowly fading tolerance. Things never end up inside a cube, but food let go over the crate goes inside it, for a norn to push the crate open. Tapping an item drops it in the middle of the view. Your basket holds 5 foods and refills one every 45 seconds. Bushes grow food on their own: drop a food on a bush and it grows that food from then on, one every 140 seconds, two at a time. Grapes contain three bites and can be carried. Persimmons must be picked before eating. Candy fills the stomach without nourishing the body. Weighted limb snares catch a paw and can be released by tapping them with Move; they are not grabbable anchors. Nine bushes keep four norns well fed. Drag a bush off the world to pull it up. All objects share one visible 2D world with the Norns. Drop an item where you see it; it falls onto the physical surface beneath it.

Care & recovery: Padded nests cushion landings, warming beds and quiet refuges calm Norns, recovery cots help heal injuries, food dispensers restock, and the sanctuary provides unusually strong support. The startle bell and hard plate are contrasting adverse tools. Effects require actual proximity to the placed object; they do not change memories or learned trust directly. Move or remove any station using the Hand in Move mode.

Egg maker

Enhanced eggs hatch with a taught gait brain and nothing else, or with a made personality. Words after a seed do the same: fluent (knows every word), quad, biped, both, masochist, cautious, sadist, extrovert, introvert, or the name of a gait you saved.

Ground

Sliding planted feet and dragging knees cost walking reward, but ordinary foot contact does not cause continuous pain. Lifting the feet clears the scrape zone. On rough ground a knee dragging along costs the walking brain a little reward, so norns that walk on their feet do better than ones that crawl on their knees.

Ready eggs wait for a free place. Lowering the limit never removes living Norns.

💉 Injection Applet — Medical Kit

Creatures 2–style medical applet adapted to this game's existing biochemistry. Select a Norn, inspect its chemistry, choose a reagent and dose, then inject. Changes affect the live creature immediately.

Select a creature to begin.

Drive chemicals can increase or decrease needs such as pain, hunger, sleepiness, and loneliness. Nutrients and metabolic chemicals only increase. Heavy metals accumulate, damage organs over time, and can kill Norns; they clear extremely slowly. Drive adjustments do not count as learned rewards.

This is a simulation-only medical tool operating on the current biochemical model, not the complete original Creatures chemical registry.

Cravings

How each food tastes to it now

Sugar becomes glucose at once and gives a rush, then a crash that tires. Starch digests slowly. Spare glucose is stored as glycogen, and once that is full, as fat. Protein builds muscle, and muscle makes it stronger. Too much fat makes it sluggish, and no vitamins make it hurt and get irritable. Mango, avocado, bean pod and coconut are each rich in two or three nutrients, so the right three of them make a whole diet (mango, avocado and bean pod do; coconut, honey and nut do not). A sweet potato has a little of everything, like a starfruit, but so little that a norn has to eat about twice as many. Foods taste sweet, sour, bitter, savoury or rich, and how nice a taste is depends on what the body is short of: a lemon is too sour for a well-fed norn, but tastes good once it runs short of vitamins. A norn remembers how each food tasted and goes for the ones it liked; a nasty mouthful ends the meal unless it is very hungry. Protein that muscle has no room for becomes glucose, and a starving norn with no fat left breaks down its muscle. A full belly hides hunger until it empties, about four minutes. A newborn feels no hunger until its first food, but food catches its eye and draws it. If it finds none, its yolk runs out after about two and a half minutes and hunger starts anyway.

Walking and climbing

Kinematic examples are used only during upright school training, never as live walking behavior. Existing pretrained gaits have not been retrained for this teacher. Teach a norn, then save its gait: new eggs of that type hatch walking the way it does, and know nothing else. Four-leg gaits are taught by Drill, best on rough ground. An upright gait is taught at the school: the norn's upright brain walks a long flat floor about 400,000 times, nudged at first, while the world waits. Saved egg types stay in this browser. Download one as a file to keep it or load it somewhere else.

back near back far front near front far

Body height is how high the torso rides above the ground under it: about 27 standing tall, under 20 on its knees. The gait brain now feels the ground a step, two and three steps ahead, and how far above its mouth the berry it wants is. It is rewarded for closing that distance, upward as well as along.

Eggs and norns

An egg on the ground hatches after about 2 minutes of warmth, in the incubator after 12 seconds. When the population reaches your selected limit, ready eggs wait and the incubator closes.

Norns share one physical world, so they can obstruct each other. A blocked Norn can ask another to move, make space itself, seek an elevated passing area, wait, or fight. A Norn that agrees to yield may walk to a nearby raised platform, ride up while the other passes underneath, and then return. They learn from whether the path actually cleared; success is not automatic.

Drives, instincts and attention are modelled on Creatures 1 and 2, with seven drives and seven verbs. A norn sees about 520 px ahead of its face and a little behind. Nutrition is a simplified take on the C2 and C3 biochemistry; vitamins are our own addition. Cubes are solid to every point of a norn's body and to its torso; the pushable cube slides when shoved and falls off edges. Food a norn cannot get to within 12 seconds is left alone for half a minute. Inherited biology now includes allele pairs, breeding and mutation. Not modelled yet: naming things by typing, infectious disease, and the other C2 drives. Ageing, starvation deaths, grief memories and REM nightmares are simplified simulations. Remains must be dragged to the incinerator with Move; they cannot be deleted by tapping. Turning around is still a reflex that mirrors the body. Resting (half-closed eyes) is sitting still awake to get over tiredness; sleep (eyes shut, z's) runs in 9 s cycles that end in 4 s of REM (eyes flicker, more and faster z's), when young norns dream their instincts. At any age, REM is also when a norn rehearses the choices that have paid off for it, so what it has learned lasts for hours instead of wearing away. Quiet sleep consolidates emotionally significant experiences without conscious dream reports; REM produces subjective dreams that Norns may imperfectly describe after waking in their own learned language.

🧠 Brain Map — Neural Inspector

Live map of a Norn's actual motor-policy neural network. Nodes show biases; connections show learned weights (blue = positive, orange = negative). This is not a reconstruction of the original Creatures 2 lobe brain: the current simulation uses a different architecture. Select a Norn and tap a node to inspect it.

Select a Norn to inspect its network.
🎥 Research Recorder — behavior, speech, and social cause tracing

Captures the world video, a 250 ms time series, and precise event records for speech, contact, witnessing, and changes in intentions. Actual events and individual perceptions are recorded separately: being near a pet does not prove a Norn understood who performed it.

Ready. Begin recording before the first touch.

For attention experiments, record a baseline, say “Mira, come”, and watch until she arrives or abandons the goal. Command-start/end events identify outcomes and reasons; snapshots include the active command and its destination. Mark notable distractions. The recording stays local until exported. Video is optional.
